items: Every animation now has a female figure too: tap Male or Female above the animation. She is the same gold statue with a lean, muscular build, a cropped top and a high ponytail, and she does every movement, variation and GIF export. Your choice is remembered.

Shorter, clearer lines on the exercise sheet. Under the set you are about to do, the record line now reads like 🏅 185lb ×6 · 5 days ago → 7 🏆 (your best at this weight, and the number that beats it). The next-set card reads 🧠 Next 185×4 80% 🔋1: the ask, your odds, and reps left in the tank; ⚖ means it is at the weight you typed, ⏱ shows what a full rest would allow. Press and hold (or hover) any of them for the full sentence.

Smoother animations for every exercise, not only the main lifts. All 100 movement types were checked frame by frame from four sides (over 113,000 steps): limbs no longer lurch between positions, feet no longer flip, elbows and knees no longer change sides mid-rep, and the head no longer snaps as the trunk tips over. A few small flickers remain where a hand passes the hem of the shorts or a thigh muscle comes into view (side bends, hinges, Nordic curls, bird dogs, sled pushes), and a box jump still cuts back to the start of its loop.

Stability-ball exercises now show the ball: sat on, lain on, under the feet in planks and bridges, behind the back in wall squats, under the forearms for stir-the-pot, or held. Medicine-ball throws and wall balls show a ball in the hands.

More names now change the picture: deficit rows, lunges and calf raises stand on a block; seated calf raises sit with the load on the knees; box jumps can start from a seat or from the knees; alternating pulldowns, swings and push-ups work one side at a time; a kneeling leg curl leans on its pad.

The animated lifter no longer pops or flickers. Every frame of 16 movements was compared with the one before it, from four sides (about 18,000 steps), and each sudden change was traced and removed: muscles and hair now come round into view gradually, the shorts have proper hems and stay put, the shine on a limb slides across instead of swapping sides, a working muscle's glow fades in and out, and the hips settle into a deadlift lockout instead of snapping.

More exercises now look like what their name says: kneeling and half-kneeling versions are on the knees, seated versions sit, alternating curls and presses take turns arm by arm, deficit push-ups have the hands on blocks, wall sits and handstand push-ups have a wall, stability-ball versions use the ball instead of a bench, preacher curls and chest-supported rows get their pad, and a held squat is held at the bottom.

Every exercise now has the new 3D animation, not only the deadlifts: 1,913 exercises across 100 movement types (presses, rows, pulls, squats, lunges, curls, raises, core work, machines, carries, jumps, Olympic lifts, cardio machines, mobility and more). Each plays in real time for a medium-heavy load with a cue for every phase, shows the right equipment (bar, dumbbells, kettlebell, cable, band, bench, machine), and follows the variation: paused, slow and isometric versions take longer, wide and close grips move the hands, incline and decline tilt the bench.
The lifter is now a gold statue with a burnished mane, built from about three times as many shapes, with smoother muscle definition. Parts of him no longer flicker in and out as he moves.

Export any animation as a GIF: tap 🎞 Export as a GIF under the player, choose the views (one file each, or side by side), the size, smoothness and speed, then download or share it. The GIF loops in exactly the time of one rep.
On the exercise map, the neighbouring exercises now take turns showing their names, so you see all of them within a few seconds.

Deadlift animations are rebuilt (🏃 on any of the 27 deadlift variations, and in their reference entries): a golden-era bodybuilder in 3D, lit from one side with muscle definition, the working muscles glowing, the bar, plates and machines in their own colours, and the bar path drawn. Side, 3D, Front and Back views. The rep runs in real time for a medium-heavy load; pause it, drag the progress bar, slow it to ½× or ¼×, and read the cue for each phase underneath. Start, Middle and End frames let you check the positions. Other exercises keep the old figure for now.

The exercise picker is easier to use on a phone: the list fills the screen, long names wrap onto two lines, a search opens with its 🎯 best matches (exercises you have logged first) and marks the words you typed, and it opens faster.
The exercise sheet is reordered: your set rows come first, then the next-set suggestion and targets, then the grade and advice, with the tips tabs at the bottom.
Count your reps out loud: tap 🔢 on the exercise sheet and say “one, two, three…”. The count shows live, “done” logs it, and the coach talks you in as a record gets close (“One more for a record!”).

A quiet notice when your pace drifts: once a workout, if your rests stretch well past your earlier pace, you get a short notice and a small 🫥 in the top bar. The app learns the minute you usually drift and gives a heads-up before it. Switch it off in Settings › Workout.

Every exercise now says where it comes from: the Full tab (and the reference entry) opens with its origin: the training system, the place, who is credited and roughly when. Named lifts get their own history (the Arnold press, the Romanian deadlift, the Pallof press, the machine brands, yoga poses and more); the rest show their movement's origin. Dates are approximate.
Search for an exercise outside the app: “🔎 Search the web” and “▶ Search videos” in the exercise tips and the reference open your browser's search in a new tab.

Trend charts are easier to read: a labelled value axis, dates along the bottom, faint dots for each session under a smoothed line, the best point ringed and the latest value at the end. Group trends (a muscle, a category) are now an index where 100 is where each exercise started, so mixing a heavy lift with a light one no longer makes the line jump about.

New 🧭 App explorer milestones in Trends › Milestones: badges for finding your way around the app (your first plan, 25 exercises explored, a gym on the map, cloud sync and more), each with a “Try it” that takes you there, and a short notice when you earn one.

The media gallery has a Sources list: the creators the cowork agent may take clips from. The new media-sources channel proposes sources and audits the ones you approved; media-gallery adds clips for the exercises you train, only from approved sources.

The anatomy chart in the glossary is now drawn in layers, front and back: the skeleton, the deep muscles and the surface muscles, with labels. Switch each layer on or off; tap any muscle for its glossary entry. (A chart image you uploaded before is kept but no longer shown.)

The end-of-workout report now says what kind of workout it was (its archetype, with the mix of strength, hypertrophy, endurance and so on), how many new bests it set, its volume against your recent workouts and the muscles that did the most work.
Plans show their archetype and mix in the start dialog, before you begin.
New 🌌 Map tab in the exercise tips: the archetypes this exercise feeds at your usual reps, and a peek at its nearest neighbours on the constellation (tap one for its card).
The live session heatmap has two more views: “Left in plan” (what the plan still has to hit) and “Off-plan” (what you did that no plan step asked for).
The constellation gives big categories more room and small ones a fair share, and 31 exercises join its leaner branches: triceps, hamstrings, calves and shins, low back, neck, jaw and breathing.

Gyms: the cowork agent can now fill in a club sheet for each club of your memberships: hours (24/7 or set), amenities, membership tiers, parking, the year it opened and its rating. For the club you use most, and any you ask about with “🔍 Ask for a deep look”, it adds first-hand member feedback (filtered to the concrete, with what it left out) and the equipment seen in recent photos. A new “Compare clubs” list sorts them by distance, rating or amenities and filters by what you need.

Exercise search is strict now: plain words search the exercise’s name, so “pallof” shows the Pallof exercises instead of every core exercise. Switch to “All fields” for the old wide search, or aim at one field: m:glute (muscle), e:cable (equipment), f:row (movement), d: (description), bp: (body part), “exact phrase” in quotes, or /a pattern/. Tap ? beside the switch for the list. When no name matches, the search widens on its own and says so.

New mobility map on the Volume page, under the heatmap: stretching, foam rolling and mobility drills colour the body areas they reach (knees and ankles as rings), with the sets per area and the areas you haven’t worked for two weeks.

The muscle map now covers grip, neck and jaw: forearm flexors and extensors, the neck front and back, and the jaw muscle light up from grip, neck and jaw training, and they have their own rows in weekly volume. Wrist curls now count for the forearms instead of the biceps’ brachialis.
The coach no longer spells out “G. O.”: words in capitals are now said as words.
Each coach has several ways to say each line, so it repeats itself less, and three new coaches join: The Commentator, Old-School Iron and The Stoic.

New coach lines you can switch on in Settings › Coach: workout start and end, plan complete, a word halfway through a longer rest, and a nudge when rest runs a minute long. The Normal preset turns on the first three.
Tell the coach what to call you (Settings › Coach › Voice) and it uses your name now and then.
Hold the 🚀 e1RM PR or 🔁 Max reps target, like the 🎯, to switch it to another weight.
The collapsed plan card now shows the steps you still have to do, with the finished ones folded behind "show all", instead of just the progress line.

The body map is redrawn as a real muscle chart: shaped muscles instead of ovals, front and back, with each head drawn where it sits (the three delts, both biceps heads, the three triceps heads, the four quads, upper, mid and lower traps and more). Group, Muscle and Heads now colour those same muscles in finer detail. The anatomy chart uses the same drawing.

Picking a plan now tells you when you last ran it: how many days ago, how many days you have trained since, and the volume you used (1¼× and so on). It shows when you start a plan, in the plan list, in Quick Pick and on the read-only plan view, and the volume you used last time is tagged when you start.

The weight list editor can copy another exercise's weights: pick one under "Copy from" (exercises with a list you wrote come first), check the preview, then use it as is or add it to yours. Handy for machines from the same line with the same odd pin positions.

Supersets now use the normal exercise sheet: chips at the top switch between the exercises (A, B, …) like attachments do, each keeping its own sets, with targets, history, the rest timer and the number pad for whichever one you are on.
Save a superset with ☆ Save and start it again from ⇄ in the exercise list with one tap; you can also start one from the exercise you have open, which becomes A.
Fixed: the selected attachment chip was unreadable in light themes.
Switching attachment mid-exercise now applies to the sets still to come: the sets you already entered keep the attachment you did them with, and are saved under it.
When one exercise's sets use more than one attachment, the set list labels where each attachment starts.
Fixed: in a long set list you could not scroll back to set 1.

The plan steps above the exercise list are now an even list: each step's number, its first exercise (with "+3 more" when it has alternatives) and a small progress bar, all the same size. Three columns on a wide screen.
Hold the 🎯 Wt PR target to switch it to another weight that is about as close to a PR, with its odds shown. Hold again for the next; a tap still loads the weight.

Your Garmin and Strava activities and weigh-ins now come from your AI runner's combined fitness list, each workout counted once, read every time cowork checks for replies. Strength workouts link to the session you logged; runs, rides and walks from the last 30 days on appear in History as cardio. A weigh-in only fills empty fields, so anything you typed by hand stays. Sleep and recovery are not in that list yet.

AI cowork now goes through your private cloud folder instead of a folder on your computer, and your AI runner answers there. It works on any device signed in to your cloud, the phone included, and a reply taken on one device is never applied again on another. Turn it on under Settings > Cowork & Sync and press Send requests once to sign in. The old folder is no longer used; nothing in it was changed.

Dates and times now read the same way everywhere: 2026-11-21 and 14:05, year first and on a 24-hour clock. Prefer your region's style? Pick "Dates: Regional" under the font picker in Settings, once, for every app.
The coach's voice has its own dials under Settings > Coach Voice: a voice volume separate from the beeps, and a speed and pitch kept for each coach.
Sound packs: export every custom clip, with the words and sound you chose for each coach line, as one file, and import it on another device (Settings > Custom sounds).

Home Arsenal: five new 2-hour plans for training at home (Push, Pull, Lower, Upper, Full Body). They use the weighted vest, plates, EZ bar, chest expander, Power Twister, neck harness, finger band, gripper, grip ring, mace, wrist roller, Burn Machine, Perfect Pushup, ab wheel, Arm Blaster, bands, kettlebells and dumbbells, and need no rack, bench, cable or pull-up bar.

Less clutter in the exercise list: 47 single-arm and single-leg versions now sit under their exercise. Open the exercise and pick "Both arms" or "Single arm" at the top. Each version keeps its own history and records, and searching by name still finds it.

The Iron Hexagon: six new 2.5-hour plans written as one six-day split. Push, Pull, Legs, then Chest & Back, Shoulders & Arms and Legs again, 15 steps each. Hip adduction is on both leg days, every core step lets you pick dynamic abs, obliques or a static hold, and each day leads with what its twin leaves alone. Find them in your plans, or pick The Iron Hexagon in the Split Planner to lay out the week.

The plan view now lists each exercise under the step its sets counted toward. With a "pulldown or pull-up" step and a later "pulldown" step, pull-ups take the first and the pulldowns show on the second.

Your own words for the coach: tap the pencil on New record, Better than last time, the target line, Halfway and Last exercise to rewrite what is said. {set} is filled in with the set, such as 205 for 8.
The weight list for an exercise has a proper editor: a chip for each weight (tap to remove), a box to add one or a few, and from / to / step to add a whole run at once.

Cardio that comes from Strava now shows its Strava name in History, with a small outline of the route beside it for GPS activities. Only the shape is kept, never where it was. Sessions already imported fill in at the next Strava sync.
Your own sounds for anything the coach says: tap 🎵 on a line under Settings > Coach Voice and choose the voice, a clip instead, or the clip and then the voice.
Record a clip with the microphone (Record, then Stop), or upload a file as before. Either way you trim it before saving.
A moment can hold up to five clips, played in turn, each with its own volume, so the same sound does not greet every record.

Coach voice, under your control: Settings > Coach Voice now lists everything the coach can say, each with its own switch, how often it speaks, and a button to hear it. Presets (Quiet, Normal, Chatty), a shortest gap between lines and a cap per minute keep it from talking too much.
Mute the coach for 10 minutes or the rest of the workout, from the sound button at the top right.

New things the coach can say, all off until you switch them on: a new record ("New record — 205 for 8"), better than last time, what to beat when you pick an exercise, halfway through the plan, and one exercise left.

Ask your AI cowork for a plan: on the Plans page, tap "Ask cowork for a plan", describe it in as much detail as you like, and the plan it writes is added to your plans for good (not just for the day).
Plan editor fixes: the exercise search no longer types backwards, a sync no longer throws you out of the plan or wipes what you were typing, and the layout is tidier.
Plan of the Day stops going easy on you: skipped plans no longer make the next one lighter, and there is a new Effort setting (Easy, Normal, Hard) in its options.
Fix weights is clearer: pick one fix (Multiply, Squash or Change), check the preview, and press a single button. It is now also available for holds.
All weights: you can write the list of weights an exercise really has (odd pin positions, half steps), and the ones you have not used show as projected rows.
The Heavier card now shows, of all heavier weights, the set with the most reps.
Small fix: dates one day back now read "1 day ago" instead of "1 days ago", and relative times are worded correctly in every language.

Tidier exercise picker: Hack Squat Machine, Plate on Forehead, Neck Harness (Loaded), Box Squat (Westside Style) and Barbell Wrist Curl duplicated other entries and are hidden. Sets you logged under them still show in your history.

Languages: GymTracker now uses the same language setting as the other apps (under the font picker in Settings), in 16 machine-translated languages. Most screens, buttons and messages are translated now; a few sentences and the exercise library itself are still in English.
New exercise: the MTS Iso-Lateral Low Row, under Row.

Sleep analysis on the Body page, from your wearable's data: your average against what you need, the sleep debt building up, how regular your bedtime is, how much weekends shift it, your deep and REM sleep, and how training and your sleep affect each other. A 30-night chart shows each night's stages.
Your AI cowork now writes a weekly sleep review with patterns and things to try, which you review before it's added, like other cowork replies.
When you type a weight you've never logged, the ▲ Heavier card shows your most impressive heavier set, not just the nearest weight.
Fix weights can now squash every set over a weight down to it (it starts at the exercise's max), or change every set at one weight to another, to fix a typo like 296 for 295.
All weights fills in the weights you haven't logged yet, up to the exercise's max, with projected reps, when your weights clearly go up in even steps. Hide them for an exercise whose stack doesn't.

Hear an exercise's setup read aloud, part by part from your feet up to your grip and breathing: tap "Read the setup aloud" in the Brief tab, or in any Body Position table. Exercises without their own table get the setup for their movement pattern.
AI cowork replies now wait for you to review them before they change your log. Tick what to keep, discard the rest, and undo anything applied. Switch review off per channel in Settings → Cowork.
The app now starts in light or dark to match your device, until you pick a theme. Settings → Theme → Match device goes back to following it.
Settings → Data → Erase all GymTracker data now really clears everything this app keeps on the device. It always asks first, and your Google Drive copy is never touched.
New default font, Atkinson Hyperlegible, built for easy reading. Settings → Font switches to System, Serif or Monospace.
Exercise animations are clearer and anatomically right, and about 50 new movements have their own figure: sit-ups, L-sits, seated rows, thrusters, burpees, sled work, mace and club swings and more.
A workout that runs past midnight stays live, and its timers keep going.
On a computer, the app uses more of the screen, up to a comfortable width.

Added the five Freemotion Row movements, the seated low-row machine, the swing to lunge high pull, the half-kneeling blind-spot rotation, the Spartan uppercut and the partner-held floor back extension.
End Workout now takes a single tap.
Record or upload your own sound, up to 5 seconds, for a PR, a progress set, the end of a rest or the end of a workout.
With a heart-rate monitor connected, you get an estimate of calories burned.
Coach's choice: on a plan step, the coach picks the best of the filtered options for you.
The next-set card also shows the S-rank set when it is within reach.
Starting a plan offers a 1.5× volume option, and can pick the volume for you from the time you want to finish by.
More timed holds in the exercise list.

Next-set coach: a challenging but achievable target for your next set, from your history, sets so far, rest, heart rate and what is left in the plan. It sticks to weights you have used and works around one you type.
Recovery data from any wearable (sleep, HRV, resting heart rate and more) is trended and can steer the next set. You can switch any factor off.
A live grade for the current exercise, and a grade trend line across the workout at the end.
Your gym chain's locations can be filled in for you, with your gym usage history and a heat map.
An option to try pairing your heart-rate monitor whenever a workout starts.
